title: PCA, kernel PCA, MDS, and manifold embeddings

items.title: Finite centering matrices and centered data
The finite centering matrix is the orthogonal projection onto the zero-sum subspace
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, let $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$. Then $H_n^T=H_n$, $H_n^2=H_n$, $H_n\mathbf1_n=0$, and for each $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $H_nv=v-(n^{-1}\mathbf1_n^Tv)\mathbf1_n$. Thus $H_n$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\mathbf1_n^Tv=0\}$.

items.title: Rank-q principal component analysis by Frobenius reconstruction error
The maximum trace over q-dimensional orthonormal frames is the sum of the top q eigenvalues
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be symmetric with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_p$, counted with multiplicity. For $1\le q\le p$ and every $Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ satisfying $Q^TQ=I_q$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(Q^TAQ)\le\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_j.$$

Equality is attained by taking the columns of $Q$ to be orthonormal eigenvectors for the $q$ largest eigenvalues. Equality holds exactly when the column space of $Q$ contains every eigenspace with eigenvalue greater than $\lambda_q$, is orthogonal to every eigenspace with eigenvalue less than $\lambda_q$, and uses a subspace of dimension $q-\#\{j:\lambda_j>\lambda_q\}$ from the eigenspace with eigenvalue $\lambda_q$.

items.title: The top right singular subspace minimizes rank-q PCA Frobenius reconstruction error
items.statement:
Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $n,p\ge1$, let $X_c=(I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T)X$, and let $1\le q\le p$. Write $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0$ for the singular values of $X_c$, padding by zeros after its rank. Among all $Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ with $Q^TQ=I_q$, the minimum of $\|X_c-X_cQQ^T\|_F^2$ is

$$\sum_{j=q+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2.$$

A frame is minimizing exactly when its column space contains every eigenspace of $X_c^TX_c$ with eigenvalue greater than $\sigma_q^2$, is orthogonal to every eigenspace with eigenvalue less than $\sigma_q^2$, and uses the remaining dimension inside the eigenspace with eigenvalue $\sigma_q^2$. In particular a choice of $q$ right singular vectors for the $q$ largest singular values is minimizing; ties can give different minimizing subspaces.

items.title: Kernel principal component analysis for a finite positive-semidefinite Gram matrix
Double-centering a finite positive-semidefinite Gram matrix preserves positive semidefiniteness
items.statement: Let $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric and satisfy $a^TKa\ge0$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^n$. With $H_n=I_n-n^{-1}\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^T$, the centered matrix $K_c=H_nKH_n$ is symmetric and positive semidefinite. Consequently it has an orthonormal eigenbasis and all its eigenvalues are nonnegative.

items.title: Classical multidimensional scaling from a finite dissimilarity matrix
Finite configurations with equal Gram matrices have isometric linear spans
items.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R^m$ be finite lists with $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle=\langle y_i,y_j\rangle$ for every $1\le i,j\le n$, using the standard Euclidean inner products. The assignment $\sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i\mapsto\sum_{i=1}^n c_i y_i$ is a well-defined linear isometry from $\operatorname{span}\{x_i\}$ onto $\operatorname{span}\{y_i\}$.

items.title: Double-centering Euclidean squared distances recovers their centered Gram matrix
items.statement: For every symmetric nonnegative zero-diagonal dissimilarity matrix $D$, the matrix $B=-\frac12H_nD^{\circ2}H_n$ used by classical multidimensional scaling is symmetric and has a real orthonormal eigendecomposition, though it may have negative eigenvalues. If $D_{ij}=\|z_i-z_j\|_2$ for points $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathbb R^d$, where $\|v\|_2=(\sum_{a=1}^d v_a^2)^{1/2}$, then $B=Z_cZ_c^T$ for the centered row-data matrix $Z_c=H_nZ$, so $B$ is positive semidefinite. The coordinates formed from all positive eigenvalues reproduce every pairwise distance exactly; if the requested embedding dimension is at least the number of positive eigenvalues, the truncated procedure is exact. The centered configurations obtained from $Z$ and these coordinates are related by a linear isometry between their spans, so the original configurations agree up to translation and Euclidean isometry of their affine spans.

items.title: Deterministic finite nearest-neighbor lists and graph symmetrizations
Finite ISOMAP with deterministic neighborhoods and connected-graph shortest paths
Minimum-norm affine reconstruction weights for a finite LLE neighborhood
Finite LLE affine least-squares weights have a unique minimum-norm minimizer
items.statement:
Fix $x_i\in\mathbb R^p$ and a nonempty finite neighbor list $N_i=(j_1,\ldots,j_k)$ of distinct indices. The constrained problem

$$\min_{w\in\mathbb R^k}\left\|x_i-\sum_{s=1}^k w_sx_{j_s}\right\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{s=1}^k w_s=1$$

has a nonempty affine set of minimizers, and exactly one member of that set has smallest Euclidean norm. Thus the minimum-norm rule in finite LLE defines one weight vector even when the local covariance matrix is singular. This conclusion uses no choice axiom.

items.title: Finite locally linear embedding with minimum-norm weights and a simple constant kernel
Under the simple constant-kernel condition, LLE trace minimizers are bottom positive eigenvectors
items.statement: Let $W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ satisfy $W\mathbf1_n=\mathbf1_n$, put $M=(I_n-W)^T(I_n-W)$, and assume $\ker(I_n-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1_n\}$. Let $0<\mu_1\le\cdots\le\mu_{n-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $M$ restricted to the zero-sum subspace $\mathbf1_n^\perp$. For $1\le q<n$, the minimum of $\operatorname{tr}(Y^TMY)$ over $Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$ with $Y^T\mathbf1_n=0$ and $Y^TY=I_q$ is $\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_j$. The minimum is attained by taking the columns of $Y$ to be orthonormal eigenvectors for the $q$ smallest positive eigenvalues; when eigenvalues tie, the minimizing subspace may vary inside the tied eigenspace. The trace is the sum of diagonal entries.
